utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-42-A, the Prosecutor versus Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Strugar, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can answer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated. Can we take the appearances, starting with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Michelle Jarvis appearing for the Prosecution, together with my colleague, Ms. Laurel Baig, and our case manager today, Mr. Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I would kindly ask the Defence of Mr. Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am Vladimir Petrovic, and I'm co-counsel for General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In this case, both parties have filed an appeal to the sentence passed on the sentence on the 31st of January, 2005. At the request of both parties, the Appeal Chamber permitted for the appeals to be withdrawn on the 20th of September, 2006. The appeal proceedings restarted on the 7th of June, 2007. Pending the appeals judgement, Mr. Strugar has been detained in The Hague, in the Netherlands, pursuant to provisions of Article 65 bis (P) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal. The Status Conference takes place 120 days after the appeal has been announced in order for the person in the Detention Unit to raise the matters with regard to the appeals in this case. In this case, the deadline started at the moment when the appeals proceedings were reopened. On the 31st of August this year, an order was issued to hold a status conference in this case. This is the first time that we sit as part of the appeals proceedings. Mr. Strugar, I would kindly ask you to tell me whether you have anything to draw my attention to with regard to the conditions in the Detention Unit or your health condition. You have the floor, Mr. Strugar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Strugar, could you please switch on the microphone so that we could hear your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I don't have any complaints to the conditions in the Detention Unit. As far as my health is concerned, I don't know whether you're familiar with the fact that last year I underwent a surgical procedure on my right hip, and my hip was replaced by an artificial hip. For the time being, I don't have any pain in that hip. However, my left hip is now giving me a lot of pain. The pain is acute. And I suppose that given the conditions that I am in at the moment, I will not be able to undergo another surgery at the moment, but it is pending. I'm sure I will have to be operated soon. I also suffer from a kidney disease, and I have been treated for this kidney disease in The Hague, in the Detention Unit as well as in the hospital. What is its name? I can't remember at the moment, but it doesn't really matter. The Hague hospital. I believe that it is the Queen's hospital in The Hague. There, they found out that the artificial channels that I have had come loose and this defect was repaired. Given my very serious condition, I was provisionally released for a period of two years. In the meantime, the kidney condition has improved to a certain extent. I have had another attack recently. The attack was somewhat milder with regard to the attacks that I suffered in the past. However, this kidney disease is always present. It's not going to go away. I also suffer from a prostate disease, and the Dutch doctors have provided me with medicines that are administered regularly. My prostate, especially since the weather has turned cold again, prevents me from getting a good night's rest. I've been undertaking some other measures, such as warming my feet, stomach and similar things, but that is another ailment that at the moment I'm suffering from and which makes me suffer. The cervical vertebra number 2 were impaired in an accident, and that's why I have the neck spondylosis, and I pass out from time to time as a result of that. I'm sure that you can appreciate that I am getting on in age. I am 75. All my joints are affected by rheumatism, especially my knees, that I will also have to undergo a surgery for. This would be more or less some of the more significant health complaints that I have at the moment. I believe that I have answered your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Strugar. I have noted your condition. You may be seated again. I would now like to remind you that pursuant to Rules 84 to 88 of the Rules that are relative to the regime in the Detention Unit, at any moment you can file a complaint or a request to the head of the Detention Unit or even the Registrar of the Tribunal, but as I've told you, we have noted everything that you have just told us about your health condition. When it comes to the development of the appeals proceedings, I would like to remind the parties of the order of the 23rd August of this year. In that order, the Trial Chamber states that the file in these proceedings encompasses all the submissions that the parties submitted before the appeals was withdrawn. By that order, the parties were invited to update their submissions in order to take into account the most recent developments with regard to the case law of this Tribunal from the moment the appeals was withdrawn. By a decision of the 31st of August of this year, I extended the deadline for the submissions, of the updated submissions. Unless you want to do it today, I would like to state that the parties have not submitted their amended submissions. Unless this changes, pursuant to Rules 108 and 115 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Appeal Chamber will examine the parties' submissions in the form as we are seized of them today. Would the parties like to say something about the appeals file and their submissions? First, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just in respect of Your Honour's invitation to the parties to file updated submissions, it is the Prosecution's intention to file such an updated submission, and we had understood that the deadline for doing so was today, given that the deadline in the order fell yesterday, being a non-registry day, so we were intending to file that submission by the close of business today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have heard your oral submission, and I'm turning to the Defence. Do you have any remarks with regard to the filing of the submissions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have analysed the case law that followed the period of time when the submissions in these proceedings were filed, and it is our position that it is not necessary to modify anything that we submitted during 2005 and 2006. The most recent sentence in the case of Mrksic until a few days ago has a lot of things that may -- and I say they may have an impact on our case. Since that sentence was passed only two or three days ago, towards the end of last week, we were not in a position to re-examine and analyse this sentence. And I remind everybody that that sentence is very similar to our case. The first accused in that case, General Mrksic, was also commander of an argine, just like our defendant. The type of responsibility for which he was charged and found guilty is similar to the charges against our defendant. It is possible that after a detailed analysis of this sentence, we will arrive at certain things that might be of some significance for this case and for this Appeals Chamber. What I would kindly ask the Appeals Chamber, and I may be asking for too much, but this is still my request, is to give some time in order to analyse that sentence in view of the similarities between the position of the first accused in that case and the accused in this case. And should we deem it necessary after the analysis, we will be able to supplement our appeal submissions. As I've already stated and I repeat, this happened only recently, and there was no time for any forward analysis between Friday and today. If this does not delay the appeals proceedings, which I don't think will be the case, I'm kindly asking for another postponement to allow us to analyse this sentence in the case of Prosecutor versus Mrksic. This will allow us to possibly supplement our submissions in these appeal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I take note that the Prosecution is going to submit an amended submission today, and you would like to be granted additional time in order to take into consideration the Mrksic judgement that you have just mentioned. In that case, pursuant to Rule 108, you should file a submission and state therein the rationale supporting your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what we are going to do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Pursuant to Rule 114 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and once the file -- the appeals file is complete, the trial will schedule a date for a hearing. This question has not been raised, but we are doing our best, depending on the schedules, to have the hearing in this case. It may happen in the first quarter of 2008, but it will all depend on the circumstances surrounding this case. As far as I am concerned, I have nothing else to add. The parties have spoken, and if you have nothing else to say or if you have no other questions, we may adjourn for today. Are there any questions, any comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. JARVIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's nothing further from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Jarvis. I am now addressing the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that there is a submission of ours dated 10th of May, 2007, which, as far as I know, is still unresolved, and it pertains to providing medical assistance to the accused Strugar in the Detention Unit and partly to what Mr. Strugar himself has told you today. Therefore, I don't know whether I'm required to give additional explanation relating to this request or should the Appeals Chamber deal with it as part of the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Based on the information that we have, this submission was denied on the 23rd of May this year. Therefore, if you wish so, you may submit a new request to the Appeals Chamber regarding the medical condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are going to review the situation and then give our response in an appropriate manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. There are no other questions? I would like to thank everybody. This concludes today's status conference. --- Status Conference concluded at 10.23 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
